description:
User Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64; rv:109.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/119.0

Steps to reproduce:

Using paypal.de trying to download financial reports, unknowingly translate feature in firefox enabled.

Actual results:

website is translated from german into a horribly wrong version of german, site stops to function proper. By clicking "Bericht" button it was also possible to create errors like "Node.removeChild: Der zu entfernende Knoten ist kein Kind dieses Knotens". Why is it possible that the translation feature breaks paypal so hard that we get these kind of errors?

Expected results:

Site should never have been translated.
After disable of the translation feature, site can be used normally.

The translation feature should never be enabled by default. If its enabled, there must be a very clear indication that the site is being translated by firefox.  It needs to be opt-in, as new user see the dialog of the new feature once, forget about it and then make some sites unusable.
